ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In order to study the structure and function of proteins, it is often necessary to separate and purify proteins from biological materials. A student used gel chromatography to separate and purify 3 kinds of proteins, A, B, and C, from a certain biological material, and performed SDS-polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis on the 3 purified proteins. The results are shown in the figure ("+" and "-" respectively represent the anode and cathode of the electrophoresis tank). It is known that the relative molecular mass of A is twice that of B, and both A and B are composed of one peptide chain. Answer the question: In the figure, when A, B, and C undergo SDS-polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis, what is the direction of migration? (Fill in "from top to bottom" or "from bottom to top").

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is an electrophoresis gel plate, with three lanes labeled at the top: A, B, and C. The upper right side of the gel plate is labeled "-", and the lower side is labeled "+", indicating that the cathode is above and the anode is below. The protein bands in each lane are all located at different heights in the gel. Then reason: In SDS-polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis, SDS causes proteins to bind a large amount of negative charge, so the proteins move toward the anode "+" in the electric field. Since "+" is below in the figure, the migration directions of A, B, and C are all from top to bottom.
